findings.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` claims to drop diagnostics about metadata members, but it only drops diagnostics that have a source location in another compilation. For a member of a PE-referenced type, the new `FirstOrDefault()` / `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` calls return null, so `Diagnostic.Create` gets `Location.None`. `Location.None.IsInSource` is false, so the guard `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || ...` passes and the diagnostic is reported. Concrete input: `lib` (built without the MessagePack analyzer, e.g. analyzer assets excluded, F#, or an older package) declares `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> { [Key(0)] public string Key {get;set;} public int Unkeyed {get;set;} }`; `app` uses `Item<int>` as a keyed member. On base this crashed. On head the consuming assembly gets a location-less MsgPack004 (an Error, L2) about a type it does not own. The same applies to MsgPack003/BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and other Location.None reports. This contradicts L8 (the defining assembly owns validating its own types) and breaks the app build instead of producing a clean one.
